Read out of saint.gr's page for 7 Μαΐου, which heads him «Οσιος Δαβιδ Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη», with the rank words and the clause about his teacher left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's naming clause in the entry headed „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ for 7. мај ст. ст. — „А имена су њихова: Авид, Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Иса, Издериос, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан и Шијо.“ The list carries no rank word and no epithet on any of the twelve; Преподобни heads the whole company in the heading and belongs to no one name, and the see or monastery each folder's English name keeps is nowhere on this page. So the bare forename is the whole of the form. **A widening**: the gate's existing `? "давид"` set of six becomes seven. Measured before drafting.
Read out of the calendar’s name link for 7 мая ст. ст., «Давид Гареджийский, прп.», with the rank abbreviation left off. The day’s own line declines him «Давида Гареджийского».

attestations.note: The day’s `/name/` link for him, 557, carries the life of the thirteen and nothing further, and that life names him among the twelve and in its title but gives him no paragraph of his own, where it gives one each to Зенон, Фаддей, Исидор, Михаил, Пирр and Стефан. So this reading adds the day and the company and no new fact about the man; the fuller Georgian dossier he plainly has was not opened and nothing is claimed from it. `dates` is unchanged. The day page prints no hymn under his name. azbyka.ru was not read. Read 8 October 2026.

feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 9 iunie and again on 7 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia». One attestation row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. The 7 mai line is the company of the thirteen Syrian fathers, and doxologia's life of John of Zedazeni names David of Gareji among the twelve disciples. Read 25 September 2026.

saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the company, and it is plainly the same company: John out of Syria and the twelve chosen to go into Iberia, whose names the page prints as «Σίω, Δαβίδ, Αντώνιος, Θαδδαίος, Στέφανος, Ισήδωρος, Μιχαήλ, Πύρρος, Ζήνων, Ισέ, Ιωσήφ και Άβιβος». **Thirteen head lines, thirteen names, so thirteen folders**, and the corpus already holds every one of them, so the whole company is upgrades and no folder is created. **`shio-of-mgvime` is the one exception and is not touched**: its `greek` row is already `venerated`, on 4 Φεβρουαρίου, so a reader may not move it; that he is listed here too is a second Greek day and is left in the report. **The Greek adds the whole story of the mission and no years at all**: the flight deeper into the desert when the crowds broke his stillness, the Theotokos appearing in a dream and commanding him to choose twelve and go to Iberia, the names written on separate papers and laid on the holy table, the night of prayer, the twelve papers an angel took from the altar into his hands before them all, the monk Euthymius left as abbot of the skete, the angel warning Bishop Eulogius of the Georgian capital of their coming, the bishop going out with clergy and people to meet them, the wonder like Pentecost by which John spoke Georgian, and their preaching through all Georgia and their veneration of the blessed places Saint Nina had passed, whom the page sends to 14 Ιανουαρίου. **No year, no hymn**, and the page does not say where any of the twelve settled afterwards — the sees and monasteries in their corpus names come from the Romanian side and nothing here is added to them. His head line is «Οσιος Δαβιδ Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη» and the page gives him no epithet, no cave and no Gareji; the folder's Romanian side supplies those and nothing here is added to them.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.05.2026 (7. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“

attestations.note: **The heading names nobody and the body enumerates the whole company, so the citation above is the heading whole** — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ — per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4's synaxis ruling and the coordinator's first ruling for an enumerated company, and the Serbian name form is read out of the body's naming clause: „А имена су њихова: Авид, Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Иса, Издериос, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан и Шијо.“ — twelve bare forenames, no rank word on any of them and no epithet, with Началник свих ових ... био је свети Јован Зедазнијски standing before the list for their leader. **The identification is the set and not the name**: the corpus already keeps these thirteen men together on this very menologion day, out of doxologia's «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia» and saint.gr's «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού», and the Prologue's twelve names map one-to-one onto the twelve folders, eleven of them unmistakably — Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан, Шијо, Иса for Ise of Tsilkani and Издериос for Isidore of Samtavisi — which forces the twelfth, Авид for Abibus of Nekresi, because it is the only slot and the only name left. **`types` was deliberately not touched on any of the thirteen.** Преподобни in that heading heads a company of thirteen whose own folders carry ranks three other calendars gave them — `hieromartyr` and `bishop` for Abibus, `hierarch` and `bishop` for Jesse, `stylite` for Anthony — and a rank word covering a whole company is not evidence about one man's own grade; adding it could make `honorific.js` compose a different word to every reader, which is the `boris-michael-of-bulgaria` ruling. **No `locations` were taken**: Georgia is a country. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **NO DATE WAS TOUCHED**: this folder already holds a date from another calendar, and a century covering the whole mission would not sharpen it; the entry's „У VI веку“ is recorded in the appended paragraph and nothing was written into `dates`. **A SECOND DAY ON THIS CHURCH, ADDED 5 October 2026, AND THE BOOK ITSELF SAYS SO.** The Prologue keeps him **again** on the Julian 27 May, in an entry of his own headed „Свети Давид Гареџијски“ — Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.06.2026 (27. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети Давид Гареџијски“ — and **that entry opens by sending the reader back to this very day**: „Овај Давид беше један од тринаест отаца грузијских (в. 7. мај)“, see 7 May. **So the identification of the two entries is the book’s own and not this reader’s**, which is the cleanest form a second-day note has taken in this wave. `BRIEF.md` §4 allows a reader to write this note on a row that is already `venerated`, under `replace_venerated: true`, and **the row above is copied back byte for byte** — same day, same month, same source, same year, the whole of the paragraph above unaltered. **No second row was made and no day was moved**: one attestation row per church is the schema, this church’s row stays on the Julian 7 May, and he does not render on the 27 May. **He gains no new name form**: the `sr` form «Давид» is already stored off the 7 May body’s naming clause and the 27 May heading prints the identical personal name, measured with `foldchk.py`. **AND THE 27 MAY ENTRY GIVES NO YEAR AT ALL**, so the `death` of 550 to 600 this folder holds from another calendar is neither corroborated nor widened and `dates` is untouched. **MOST OF THE 27 MAY ENTRY IS ALREADY IN THIS LIFE, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE READING.** The three stones, the angel to Elias the patriarch of Jerusalem, the command that two be returned and one is blessing enough, and the whole grace of the Holy Land carried off in them are all here already, out of the pages read in September. **A second book telling the same story the same way is worth recording and changes nothing.** **What is new**: that he was called Гареџијски **after the Gareji wilderness near Tiflis**, where he struggled; that **he left the monastery in the charge of the elders Lucian and Dodo** when he set out — the existing life has Lucian as his disciple and does not put Dodo in charge with him; that at the hill from which Jerusalem could be seen **he wept and said „Како да се дрзнем ја да својим грешним ногама ходим по стопама Богочовека?“**, how shall I dare walk with my sinful feet in the footsteps of the God-man, and **sent his disciples on as the worthier**; that the angel told the patriarch to send **after the elder who is returning to Syria**, where the existing life has only that he is going away from the city; and that **the third stone lies on his grave to this day and has a wonderworking power of healing**. **`related` UNTOUCHED, AND BOTH ELDERS WERE CHECKED.** `dodo-of-gareji` is already in this folder’s `related` in both directions, so the Dodo of this entry needs no new row. **Лукијан gains no folder and no row**: the corpus keeps six Lucians and not one of them is this disciple — `lucian-of-antioch`, `lucian-of-tomis`, `lucian-of-the-kyiv-caves`, `lucian-17-october`, `lucian-fedotov` and `lucianus-companion-of-peregrinus` — and by the coordinator’s third ruling nothing is minted for him; he is named in the prose of this life already. **Илија, патријарх јерусалимски, gains nothing either**: the corpus keeps twenty-three men of that name and no patriarch of Jerusalem among them. `types` untouched — `venerable`, `ascetic`, `hermit` and `wonderworker` are all four corroborated by this entry, the last of them by the healing stone. **No `locations`**, although Tiflis and the Gareji wilderness are named here for the first time, and that is the one thing this entry would make possible and which is left for the author. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
